extracted.intended_audience: trade mark applicants, proprietors, agents/solicitors, and Patent Office officials (UK, under the Patents, Designs and Trade Marks Act 1883)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules, required forms, fees, and classification guidance for applying, opposing, certifying, and maintaining trade marks under the Patents, Designs and Trade Marks Act 1883 (UK). Includes form text, submission/formatting requirements, and the classes of goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security (bond) for costs on opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Comptroller-General requires security for costs under the Act and Rules, the opposing parties must enter into an obligation (bond) as security for such costs as may be awarded in respect of such opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The condition: if the obligors (or any of them) or their heirs/executors/administrators do and shall well and truly pay all such costs as the High Court of Justice shall think fit to award, then the obligation is void; otherwise it remains in full force. The bond is to be signed, sealed and delivered and is to state the penal sum in pounds. See Form F (Bond).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant may object to solvency of security
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the opposing party is required to bring an opposition matter before the Court under Rule 29, the Applicant is afforded an opportunity of objecting, if he thinks fit, to the solvency of the security for the costs which may be awarded in respect of the opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This must be done prior to the matter being brought before the Court (see para. 34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees must accompany application in impressed stamps
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for the registration of a Trade Mark will not be entered by the Comptroller unless it is accompanied by the proper fees in impressed stamps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See para. 36 and the First Schedule of Fees; 'All fees must be paid by stamped form.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Cutlers' Company jurisdiction for certain goods
rubrics_metrics.description: By s.81(3) of the Act, applications for registration of Trade Marks used on cutlery, edge tools, raw steel, goods made of steel or of steel and iron combined (with or without a cutting edge) made by a person carrying on business in Hallamshire, or within six miles thereof, shall be made to the Cutlers' Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rules 53–56 and para. 14. Applications to the Cutlers' Company should be made on the specified form with the left-hand corner address 'To the Cutlers Company, Sheffield' and left at or sent to Cutlers Hall, Sheffield. Include an unstamped copy on foolscap paper (Rule 53). Postal address and Law Clerk contact provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manchester Trade Marks Office for cotton classes / search fees
rubrics_metrics.description: An office will be opened at 48 Royal Exchange, Manchester to facilitate recording of Trade Marks used in respect of Cotton Goods; searches can be made there for Marks in textile classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches charged at 1s for each quarter of an hour for all Marks in classes of Textiles from Class 23 to Class 35.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Comptroller's Certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Comptroller's Certificate in relation to a Trade Mark is of four kinds: (i) for use in legal proceedings; (ii) for use in applying for registration in Foreign Countries; (iii) of any application made and proceedings thereon; (iv) a certificate of refusal of a Mark in use before 13th August 1875 and not registerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain any of these certificates forward the appropriate Form (e.g., Form 'E', Form 'S', Form 'Ty', Form 'Z') with the Comptroller's official number of the Mark and state purpose. The form must be accompanied by two unmounted copies of each Mark for which a Certificate is required (see paras. 39–41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of unmounted copies for cotton/coloured marks
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Certificate is required in respect of a Cotton Mark, or where the representations/specimens in the application are coloured, two unmounted copies of the Mark must be supplied agreeing in every respect with the representations forming part of the Application for Registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special attention must be paid to this requirement because the Certificate cannot be prepared until the unmounted copies are received by the Comptroller (para. 41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of subsequent proprietors — Form and declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request and Declaration to be made by a subsequent Proprietor on application for registration in his name of a registered Trade Mark must be made on Form 'A'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See para. 42 and the Second Schedule Forms listing; the application must be supported by the specified declaration and particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees schedule and specific fee items
rubrics_metrics.description: The First Schedule lists fees for many actions (application, registration, entry of opposition, continuance at 14 years, inspection, searches, certificates, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: application to register for one class 0s 5d; registration fee 10s; entering notice of opposition 10s; continuance at expiration of 14 years 10s; for inspecting register per quarter hour 0s 10d; searches among classified representations per quarter hour 0s 10d; making an office copy per 100 words (never less than 1s) etc. All fees to be paid by stamped form. See First Schedule for full list and amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application representation format and mounting
rubrics_metrics.description: One representation to be fixed within the square on the application, and two others to be sent on separate sheets of foolscap. Representations of larger size may be folded but must be mounted upon linen and affixed thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Form F (Application for Registration). Follow exact mounting/folding guidance to ensure proper handling (Form notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: State prior use if mark used before 13 August 1875
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Trade Mark has been in use in respect of the goods since before 13th August 1875, the application must state the length of such user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note on the application Form (see para. 58/Form F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Goods in application must be within one class; separate application per class
rubrics_metrics.description: Only goods contained in one and the same class should be set out in the 'in respect of' section of an application; a separate application form is required for each separate class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit note on the Application Form (Form F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign the application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application is to be signed by the applicant; in the case of a firm by a partner (adding 'A member of the firm'); in the case of a company by the Secretary or other principal officer (adding 'For the Company'); or an agent may sign (adding 'Agent').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed signature formulations on the Form (Form F notes d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Board of Trade — document formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal statements to the Board of Trade should be written on foolscap paper (one side only) with a margin of two inches on the left-hand side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Form H (Appeal to Board of Trade) and para. 62; adhere to paper/margin/one-side requirement for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Opposition — unstamped duplicate and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Opposition to an application for registration must be accompanied by an unstamped duplicate and must state the grounds of opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice must be dated and signed at the end by the opponent or his solicitor and addressed to the Comptroller (Form J and para. references; see s.69).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to enter subsequent proprietor — particulars and solemn declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: A Request to enter the name of a subsequent proprietor must include a declaration that the applicant is entitled to the Trade Mark and goodwill, state how transfer occurred (death, marriage, assignment, operation of law, etc.), and comprise every material fact/documents affecting proprietorship; it must be a solemn declaration made conscientiously and attested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form includes fields for particulars, signature, date, and attestation before an authority. Note stamping requirements under Statutory Declarations Act if declaration made outside the UK (see Form). See s.87 and Trade Marks Rules 84–88.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Certificate of Refusal for old marks
rubrics_metrics.description: To request a Certificate of Refusal to register a Trade Mark in use before 13 August 1875, the Applicant should forward the specified form with mark details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Form (Request for Certificate of Refusal) and s.77 references; signature and dating required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of alteration of address on the Register
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered proprietor who desires that his address on the Register be altered must give notice in the prescribed form specifying the registered Trade Mark number, class, and the new address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Notice of Application for Alteration of Address form; see Trade Marks Rules 46.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Order for rectification — enclose office copy of Court Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Court Order directs rectification of the Register entry, notice must be given enclosing an office copy of the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be signed by the person interested or his agent; refer to s.90(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by proprietor to cancel entry on Register
rubrics_metrics.description: A proprietor may apply to have the entry or part of the entry of a Trade Mark on the Register cancelled by submitting the prescribed form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Form O (Application to Cancel Entry). Note: neither the Act nor Rules deal specifically with cancelling marks; see s.79(5) and Trade Marks Rules 45 for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration in support of application for cancellation — required statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration in support of cancellation must state (1) that the application signed and dated is true; (2) that the declarant is the person whose name appears on the Register as proprietor (or member of the registered firm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration is to be made conscientiously under the Statutory Declarations Act and attested; note stamp requirement (28s. 6d. impressed Inland Revenue stamp) if made before a Commissioner to administer oaths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for correction of clerical error
rubrics_metrics.description: A prescribed Request form exists to ask the Comptroller to correct a clerical error in regard to a Trade Mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the Request to the Comptroller, Trade Marks Branch, with particulars of the error and signature (Form P).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Certificate of Registration for use abroad — state country
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered proprietor requesting a Certificate of Registration for use in obtaining registration abroad must state the name of the country in which registration is to be sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed form (Form E) and include the country and signature; see s.91 and para. references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Certificate of Registration for use in legal proceedings — state exact title
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered proprietor requesting a Certificate of Registration for use in legal proceedings must state the exact title of the legal proceedings for which the certificate is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed form (Form S) and include the full title of proceedings; see Trade Marks Rules 57.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for settlement of a special case
rubrics_metrics.description: If parties are unable to agree upon facts on which the Court's opinion is to be taken, they may apply for settlement of a special case requesting the Comptroller to fix a day to attend and obtain findings on the matters of fact to be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form T to be signed by both parties; see Trade Marks Rules 43.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Certificate of Comptroller as to application
rubrics_metrics.description: A Request form allows an applicant to ask the Comptroller to furnish a certificate as to certain particulars of the application for registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out the particulars which the Comptroller is requested to certify on the form and sign (Form U).

rubrics_metrics.name: General Certificate of Comptroller-General
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller-General can issue a general Certificate as to an application for or registration of a Trade Mark under s.96.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form V and internal procedure referenced (see s.96).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for copy of official notification of registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered proprietor may request a copy of the official notification of the registration of the Trade Mark by forwarding the prescribed form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form V (Request for Copy of Official Notification) — include mark number, class, proprietor name and signature; see s.88.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from Cutlers' Company to Comptroller — format and duplicate
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal against the decision of the Cutlers' Company must be accompanied by an unstamped duplicate and the statement of the case on foolscap, one side only, with a two-inch left margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form W and address to the Comptroller; see s.81.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-statement (applicant's response to opposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: In reply to a Notice of Opposition, the Applicant may file a Counter-statement giving the grounds relied on for the Application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counter-statement must be dated and signed by the Applicant or his Solicitor and sent to the Comptroller (Form X). See s.69 references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form content and required wording for bond/obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bond form sets out the parties, the penal sum (in pounds), the condition that the obligors are bound firmly and jointly and severally to the Comptroller-General, sealed with their seals, dated, and the detailed recital of the application/opposition matter, and the standard conditional clause as to payment of costs awarded by the High Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the Bond contains the recitals identifying the application/opposition numbers and parties, is properly executed, and follows the prescribed wording in the Forms schedule (Form F/Bond).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification general note — mixed-material goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Any wares made of mixed materials (e.g., of both cotton and silk) shall be included in such one of the classes appropriated to those materials as the registrar may desire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general allocation principle: the registrar has discretion to place mixed-material wares in the class he deems appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 1 — Chemical substances used in manufactures, photography, or philosophical research, and anti-corrosives
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 1 covers chemical substances used in manufactures, photography, or philosophical research, and anti-corrosives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Acids (including vegetable acids), Alkalies, Artists' colours, Pigments, Mineral dyes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 2 — Chemical substances used for agricultural, horticultural, veterinary, and sanitary purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 2 covers chemical substances used for agricultural, horticultural, veterinary, and sanitary purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Artificial manure, Cattle medicines, Deodorisers, Vermin destroyers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 3 — Chemical substances prepared for use in medicine and pharmacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 3 covers chemical substances prepared for use in medicine and pharmacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cod liver oil, Medicated articles, Patent medicines, Plasters, Rhubarb.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 4 — Raw or partly prepared vegetable, animal, and mineral substances used in manufactures (not included in other classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 4 includes raw or partly prepared vegetable, animal, and mineral substances used in manufactures not included in other classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Resins, Oils used in manufactures and not included in other classes, Dyes (other than mineral), Tanning substances, Fibrous substances (cotton, hemp, flax, jute), Wool, Silk, Bristles, Hair, Feathers, Cork, Seeds, Coal, Coke, Bone, Sponge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 5 — Unwrought and partly-wrought metals used in manufacture
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 5 covers unwrought and partly-wrought metals used in manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Iron and steel (pig or cast), iron rough bar and rail, bolt and rod, sheet and boiler and armour plates, hoop, lead pig/rolled/sheet, wire, copper, zinc, gold in ingots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 6 — Machinery of all kinds and parts (except agricultural/horticultural machines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 6 covers machinery of all kinds and parts of machinery, except agricultural and horticultural machines included in Class 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Steam engines, Boilers, Pneumatic machines, Hydraulic machines, Locomotives, Sewing machines, Weighing machines, Machine tools, Mining machinery, Fire engines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 7 — Agricultural and horticultural machinery and parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 7 covers agricultural and horticultural machinery and parts of such machinery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Ploughs, Drilling machines, Heaping machines, Thrashing machines, Chums, Cyder presses, Chaff cutters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 8 — Philosophical and scientific instruments and apparatus for useful purposes; instruments and apparatus for teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 8 covers philosophical instruments, scientific instruments, and apparatus for useful purposes, and instruments/apparatus for teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Mathematical instruments, Gages, Logs, Spectacles, Educational appliances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 9 — Musical instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 9 covers musical instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (list implied under musical instruments category).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 10 — Horological instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 10 covers horological instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: clocks, watches, and related horological items (implied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 11 — Instruments, apparatus, and contrivances for surgical/curative purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 11 covers instruments, apparatus, and contrivances, not medicated, for surgical or curative purposes, or in relation to the health of men or animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Bandages, Friction gloves, Lancets, Enemas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 12 — Cutlery and edge tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 12 covers cutlery and edge tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Knives, Forks, Scissors, Shears, Files, Saws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 13 — Metal goods not included in other classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 13 covers metal goods not included in other classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Anvils, Keys, Basins (metal), Needles, Hoes, Shovels, Corkscrews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 14 — Goods of precious metals and jewellery
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 14 covers goods of precious metals (including aluminium, nickel, Britannia metal, etc.) and jewellery and their imitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Plate, Clock cases and pencil cases of such metals, Sheffield and other plated goods, gilt and ormolu work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 15 — Glass
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 15 covers glass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Window and plate glass, Painted glass, Glass mosaic, Glass beads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 16 — Porcelain and earthenware
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 16 covers porcelain and earthenware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: China, Stoneware, Terra Cotta, Statuary porcelain, Tiles, Bricks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 17 — Manufactures from mineral and other substances for building or decoration
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 17 covers manufactures from mineral and other substances for building or decoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cement, Plaster, Imitation marble, Asphalt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 18 — Engineering, architectural, and building contrivances
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 18 covers engineering, architectural, and building contrivances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Diving apparatus, Warming apparatus, Ventilating apparatus, Filtering apparatus, Lighting contrivances, Drainage contrivances, Electric and pneumatic bells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 19 — Arms, ammunition, and stores (not included in Class 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 19 covers arms, ammunition, and stores not included in Class 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cannon, Small-arms, Fowling pieces, Swords, Shot and other projectiles, Camp equipage, Equipments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 20 — Explosive substances
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 20 covers explosive substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Gunpowder, Gun-cotton, Dynamite, Fog-signals, Percussion caps, Fireworks, Cartridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 21 — Naval architectural contrivances and naval equipments (not in Classes 19 and 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 21 covers naval architectural contrivances and naval equipments not included in Classes 19 and 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Boats, Anchors, Chain cables, Rigging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 22 — Carriages
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 22 covers carriages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Railway carriages, Waggons, Railway trucks, Bicycles, Bath chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 23 — Cotton yarn and thread
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 23 covers cotton yarn and thread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Sewing cotton on spools or reels, Sewing cotton not on spools or reels, Dyed cotton yams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 24 — Cotton piece goods of all kinds
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 24 covers cotton piece goods of all kinds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cotton shirtings, Long cloth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 25 — Cotton goods not included in Classes 23, 24, or 38
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 25 covers cotton goods not included in Classes 23, 24, or 38.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cotton lace, Cotton braids, Cotton tapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 26 — Linen and hemp yarn and thread
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 26 covers linen and hemp yarn and thread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (class list continues with linen/hemp items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 27 — Linen and hemp piece goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 27 covers linen and hemp piece goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (as appropriate to linen/hemp piece goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 28 — Linen and hemp goods not included in Classes 26, 27, and 50
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 28 covers linen and hemp goods not included in Classes 26, 27, and 50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (items of linen/hemp goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 29 — Jute yarns and tissues, and other articles made of jute not included in Class 30
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 29 covers jute yarns and tissues and other articles made of jute not included in Class 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (jute-related goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 30 — Silk (spun, thrown, or sewing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 30 covers silk, spun, thrown, or sewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (silk materials and related goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 31 — Silk piece goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 31 covers silk piece goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (silk piece goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 32 — Other silk goods not included in Classes 30 and 31
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 32 covers other silk goods not included in Classes 30 and 31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (other silk articles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 33 — Yarns of wool, worsted, or hair
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 33 covers yarns of wool, worsted, or hair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (yarns and related products).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 34 — Cloths and stuffs of wool, worsted, or hair
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 34 covers cloths and stuffs of wool, worsted, or hair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (cloths, stuffs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 35 — Woollen, worsted and hair goods not included in Classes 33 and 34
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 35 covers woollen, worsted, and hair goods not included in Classes 33 and 34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (finished woollen goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 36 — Carpets, floor-cloth, and oilcloth
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 36 covers carpets, floor-cloth, and oilcloth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Drugget, Mats and matting, Rugs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 37 — Leather, skins (unwrought and wrought), and articles made of leather
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 37 covers leather and skins (unwrought and wrought) and articles made of leather not included in other classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Saddlery, Harness, Whips, Portmanteaus, Furs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 38 — Articles of clothing (ready-made)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 38 covers articles of clothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Hats of all kinds, Caps and bonnets, Hosiery, Gloves, Boots and shoes, Other ready-made clothing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 39 — Paper (except paper-hangings), stationery, and book-binding
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 39 covers paper (except paper-hangings), stationery, and book-binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Envelopes, Sealing wax, Pens (except gold pens), Ink, Playing cards, Blotting cases, Copying presses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 40 — Goods manufactured from india-rubber and gutta-percha
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 40 covers goods manufactured from india-rubber and gutta-percha not included in other classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (rubber/gutta-percha manufactured goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 41 — Furniture and upholstery
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 41 covers furniture and upholstery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Paper hangings, Papier-mâché, Mirrors, Mattresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 42 — Substances used as food or ingredients in food
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 42 covers substances used as food or as ingredients in food.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cereals, Pulses, Olive oil, Hops, Malt, Dried fruits, Tea, Sago, Salt, Sugar, Preserved meats, Confectionery, Oil cakes, Pickles, Vinegar, Beer clarifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 43 — Fermented liquors and spirits
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 43 covers fermented liquors and spirits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Beer, Cyder, Wine, Whisky, Liqueurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 44 — Mineral and aerated waters (natural and artificial), including ginger-beer
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 44 covers mineral and aerated waters, natural and artificial, including ginger-beer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Mineral waters, aerated waters, ginger-beer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 45 — Tobacco (manufactured or unmanufactured)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 45 covers tobacco, whether manufactured or unmanufactured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (tobacco and related products).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 46 — Seeds for agricultural and horticultural purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 46 covers seeds for agricultural and horticultural purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (various seeds).
